# Campaign Channel Discovery

- Discovery is operator-triggered background work, single-flighted per campaign; the operator names the accounts that read (`account_ids`, required). Reservation is all-or-nothing: every picked account is checked against one fleet snapshot, then locked in sorted id order under warming's lifecycle lock and re-asked from every holder inside it; the first failing account refuses the start and is named. Warming, the listener and a run exclude each other; neuroshilling sits outside that circle. Do not hold the lifecycle locks across the run.
- The reserved accounts form one pool, and each is ONE concurrent stream: a scheduler hands queued jobs to per-account workers, each pacing only between its own reads, so a run's duration divides by the pool size. Recommendation, seed and post-page jobs prefer a Premium account while one can still read (non-premium gets FLOOD_PREMIUM_WAIT and a tenth of the recommendations); no Premium in the pool skips the post wave as `premium_required`. Each account may spend at most `discovery_max_reads_per_run` wave reads — past that it stops taking wave jobs (truncation, not a stop) but still probes, bounded by `limit`. An account that floods, cools, fails `discovery_max_consecutive_errors` reads in a row, or whose client never connected (`unavailable` → `offline`, dropped at once) leaves the pool; a read a flood or a connection failure killed is requeued ONCE for another account (the failure is recorded only if the retry never ran). The run stops only when the pool is empty, labelled by the reason the last account left; `last_error` is the first FAILED source (a cooldown stop overrides it). Health is re-read before every read. Live progress (`DiscoveryProgress.work`) is in-memory only.
- Sources: keyword search, the global post search (paged, narrower than its docs suggest), recommendations for the operator's seed and for the sweep's best CHANNEL hits — recommendations return channels only, so a groups search skips both recommendation waves as `kind_unsupported`. A chosen category appends its word bundle to the sweep. `kind` is decided once, at the gateway. `hide_seen` and `limit` act in the merge; `seen` is keyed by the case-folded handle and written at the END of a run over the rows the board shows as judged (`qualified_at` set, probe not failed) — a row a stopped pass left pending or unanswered is not marked, so the re-run resumes it. A re-run whose every hit is already seen keeps the previous rows instead of wiping them and ends `done` without qualification. `language`, `comments`, `access` open-vs-join-request and `category` need `about`/`join_request` from GetFullChannel: the linked-group cache stores both (an upsert keeps each fact it did not learn), so a fresh row settles from cache through the same admission as a probe and only a legacy row missing the fact is probed. A rejected row is DELETED, never stored hidden; counts land in the run report's `filtered`. Unknown values never reject (an access the probe could not establish is `None`, not `open`); groups are never rejected by the comments filter (they have no verdict) and are shown `not_adoptable`. A username-less recommendation is stored as `id:<channel_id>` with access `subscription`, never probed, never adoptable, and rejected by `comments = on`. Subscriber bounds apply once counts are known, never to recommendation seeds. An unresolvable seed is a refusal, never an empty answer.
- A run's waves share one read budget of `discovery_max_reads_per_run × pool size`; job order puts keywords first, then the operator's seed, post pages, recommendations, and the recommendation share is held back from the start (streams run concurrently, so wave order alone no longer protects it). The post wave caps its own total by reserving reads on enqueue. Truncation is reported and is NOT a run error. The rolling-24h search allowance is separate. Wave shape is a module literal, not a setting; the candidate cap is the request's `limit` alone.
- Whether a read failure is a rate limit is the gateway's `kind`, never the reason text; a limit with no duration takes the configured no-duration cooldown.
- Merge interleaves per OUTCOME, not per source, before the cap: source priority decides dedup spelling, not which source fills the cap.
- Every source reports `ran`/`failed`/`skipped`; `hits` are DISTINCT usable channels. Replace stored candidates only when at least one source answered; an EMPTY result additionally needs the keyword sweep itself to have answered and nothing dropped as seen. A run stopped by a flood or a cooldown never displaces the stored set. Per-run progress, provenance and verdict fields are ephemeral across restart; `kind`, the seen table and the cached `about`/`join_request` are the persisted exceptions.
- Keyword suggestion is not part of a run: no campaign, no account, no Telegram read; single WORDS; DeepSeek only; an unusable answer is a 200 carrying a code.
